Both inputs read in full, plus the path/tier checks needed to make the manifest real. Four things I found change the plan's shape — flagged inline where they land.

---

# Cart bundle (SFCC-11) — executable build plan

## 1. Goal statement

Build the Zimmermann cart drawer and its line-item system — SFCC-315, 270, 795, 271, 272, 250, 275 — as prescribed by those seven Sprint 5 cards, as designed in Figma file `QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs` nodes `9323-65888/65895/65983/66104` (DEFAULT PAGE TEMPLATE) plus the CART MERGE, WISHLIST, INTERNATIONAL, EMPTY BAG and OOS state groups across all four breakpoints, as approached by the FED handbook and `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`, as established in PR #85 (SFCC-236 shared product card — atoms → molecules → organism, page-level mapper, `ui-kits/<name>Shared.ts`, theme registration, `desktop/`/`mobile/` e2e split), using: the **override** approach with copy-first for `product-item/` and `item-variant/` (mirrored base files exist), the **new-component** approach under `ui-kits/` for the drawer organism, quantity stepper, inline message, actions row, button group and empty state (no mirrored base file exists), **co-located `Zimm*` recipes** for all styling, and the **existing `--zimm-*` foundation untouched** — every colour and space value in this design already exists there.

---

## 2. Scale call — six branches, and how much loop each earns

> **⚠️ SUPERSEDED by §11 (Marcel, 2026-09-17): SINGLE PR, 18 commits.**
> Retained as the record of why the seams were drawn where they were. §3's file manifest and §4's
> steps remain valid verbatim — they regroup by commit instead of by branch. §5's per-step loop
> criteria remain valid; only the per-*branch* loop scaling is replaced.

### Six branches, not one PR and not seven

| # | Branch | Stories | Files | Why it is its own branch |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **B0** | `fix/SFCC-11_cart-e2e-area` | — (infra) | 1 | `.github/workflows/qa.yml` is **Tier 1 CI/CD**. Bundling it into a feature PR drags `@tier-1-approvers` onto a feature review and breaches AGENTS.md Hard Rule #10 (one protection tier per change). |
| **B1** | `feature/SFCC-315_cart-drawer` | 315 | ~7 | **Ships first and standalone.** SFCC-316 (Jhoan, same sprint, Ready for Development) composes into it. Anything that delays this branch delays someone else's active-sprint card. |
| **B2** | `feature/SFCC-270_cart-item-override` | 270 | ~14 | **The only Tier 2 code branch.** `product-item/` pulls `@pwa-squad-b @tier-2-approvers @tier-1-approvers`. Keeping it alone means one squad-B reviewer sees one coherent override, not a 40-file cart feature. Also the only branch with a mandatory copy-first pause. |
| **B3** | `feature/SFCC-795-271_cart-item-states-stepper` | 795 + 271 | ~20 | 795 and 271 are the same pixels. §5.4: "795 subsumes 270, 271 and 250's UI states — one implementation, three cards' ACs." Splitting them means building the stepper twice. |
| **B4** | `feature/SFCC-250-272_max-qty-wishlist-actions` | 250 + 272 | ~16 | **Welded, per the settled decision.** Both land in one `onAuthSuccess` callback (merge → cap → wishlist resume). They cannot be reviewed or reverted independently. |
| **B5** | `feature/SFCC-275_cart-button-group` | 275 | ~6 | Independent of the cart-item chain. Can run in parallel with B2/B3 by a second pair of hands. |

Every branch is cut fresh from an updated `develop` (`origin/develop` head `71025f18`; local is 41 behind). Never from `feature/SFCC-831-689_country-language-mismatch`, which carries open PR #112.

**Order:** B0 ∥ B1 first → B2 (copy-first pause) → B3 → B4. B5 any time after B0. B4 depends on B3's stepper existing and on B1's drawer hosting the empty state.

### One Tier 2 touch you cannot design away

Every branch that adds a recipe must edit `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` to register it. That file is inside `overrides/app/theme/components/` → **Tier 2**, `@tier-2-approvers @tier-1-approvers`. The co-location relief in CODEOWNERS (`overrides/app/components/**/*.css.ts` → squads only, last-match-wins) covers the recipe *file* and not the registration *line*. So B1, B3, B4 and B5 each carry one Tier 2 approver for a one-line import + one key. Plan for it; do not be surprised by it at PR time.

### How much loop — scaled down deliberately

| Branch | Loop | Why |
|---|---|---|
| B0 | **None.** | A workflow allow-list. Verified by observing the next cart PR's `e2e_scope` output, not by a Tester. A loop here is theatre. |
| B1 | **Light** — Tester + Scorer on one pass. | Mostly reuse: `ZimmDrawer` already owns overlay, right placement, Escape, `finalFocusRef`, mobile full-height and scroll-lock. Two things are genuinely new (the 52px reserved band, the `xLarge` width fix) and both are assertable in one `.css.test.ts`. |
| B2 | **Full loop, but only on the copy-first pass.** | The risk here is not "does it look right", it is "did the override intercept and did the 11 downstream surfaces survive". After Marcel's verification the restyle is conventional. Dropping the second loop pass. |
| B3 | **Full loop.** | Largest surface: ~25 ACs including 11 accessibility, five stepper states, three error states, two breakpoint reflows. This is where a missed state ships. |
| B4 | **Full loop, and the only step that gets a second adversarial pass.** | Async state, an auth seam, an ordered callback, a loop guard and a render guard that must not race a mutation. Highest defect cost, lowest visibility in review. |
| B5 | **Light.** | 8 ACs, six presentational, one conditional render, one stubbed destination. A two-point story does not earn a full loop. |

**Explicitly dropped, and why:** no Playwright spec on B1 (nothing to drive it — see open question 7); no `.test.ts` on the four pure-presentation atoms/molecules whose only logic is prop interpolation (`testing.md`'s single-parent exemption — covered by the organism's `play`); no separate loop pass on B2's restyle commit. Anything more would be over-scaled machinery, which is a defect in a plan.

---

## 3. File manifest

Tiers from `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md` and `protectedFiles.md`, owners read directly from `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/CODEOWNERS`. Not from `.claude/registry/*.md`.

### B0 — e2e area

| File | Action | Tier | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.github/workflows/qa.yml` | modify | **Tier 1 CI/CD** | `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers` |

> **BLOCKED.** Named explicitly in the brief, but owner approval is not confirmed. Per Hard Rule #2 the Implementer must either verify the authenticated `gh` login is in `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers` (`gh api user --jq .login`, then the team membership call) or stop and get a named approving review before touching it. Do not start B0 on an unverified session.

Add a `cart` group to `detect-changes`'s allow-lists covering `overrides/app/pages/cart/**`, `overrides/app/components/product-item/**`, `overrides/app/components/item-variant/**`, `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/**/zimmCart*/**`, `e2e/tests/zimm/cart/**`, `e2e/features/cart/**`. Note `e2e_homepage` is currently the **only** area group in the file — `testing.md`'s longer tag list is aspirational, so `cart` is the second, not the eighth.

### B1 — SFCC-315

| File | Action | Tier | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmCartDrawer/index.tsx` | create | Tier 3 | `@pwa-squad-a @pwa-squad-b` |
| `.../zimmCartDrawer/index.test.tsx` | create | Tier 3 | same |
| `.../zimmCartDrawer/index.stories.tsx` | create | Tier 3 | same |
| `.../zimmCartDrawer/zimmCartDrawer.css.ts` | create | Tier 3 (`**/*.css.ts`) | `@pwa-squad-a @pwa-squad-b` |
| `.../zimmCartDrawer/zimmCartDrawer.css.test.ts` | create | Tier 3 | same |
| `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmDrawer/zimmDrawer.css.ts` | **modify** | Tier 3 (`**/*.css.ts`) | `@pwa-squad-a @pwa-squad-b` |
| `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmDrawer/zimmDrawer.css.test.ts` | modify | Tier 3 | same |
| `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` | modify | **Tier 2** | `@tier-2-approvers @tier-1-approvers` |

### B2 — SFCC-270 (copy-first)

### B1 — SFCC-315, cart drawer organism

#### Step 1.1 — Fix `ZimmDrawer`'s `xLarge` width (this is a real bug, not a tidy-up)

**Consequence first.** `zimmDrawer.css.ts` already ships an `xLarge` size whose own comment says it is for Cart. Its value is `WIDTH_XLARGE = '82%'`. Figma's cart panel is a **fixed 1186px** at both 1440 and 1920 (§11.1; panel `x=256` on the 1440 frame and `x=736` on the 1920 frame — 1184 both times, so the *gap* grows and the panel does not). 82% of 1920 is **1574px** — 388px wider than designed. The inner composition is itself fixed (128 + 360 + 140 + 430 + 128 = 1186), so on a 1920 screen the shopper gets 388px of dead white space inside the panel, and the two-column layout sits off-centre. Build SFCC-315 on the existing variant unchanged and it is wrong on every large monitor.

**Mechanism.** The 82% came from a Figma frame annotation, and `zimmDrawer.css.ts`'s own comment records that the *previous* reading of that same annotation was already wrong once ("that frame's annotation was wrong (or superseded)"). The annotation is a percentage; the frames are a fixed width.

**Changes.** Replace `WIDTH_XLARGE = '82%'` with a rem constant equal to 1186px (`74.125rem`), applied as `width`/`maxWidth` with `maxWidth: '100%'` so it cannot exceed a narrow viewport. Keep the comment convention: cite the Figma frames, state that 82% was the annotation and 1186 is the measurement, per the `zimmButton.css.ts` house pattern.

**Pass criteria.**
1. `zimmDrawer.css.test.ts` gains an assertion that `xLarge.content` resolves to the 1186px rem value above `md`, and that `maxWidth` is `100%`.
2. No other size variant's resolved output changes — assert `large`, `tablet`, `small`, `prompt`, `mobile` snapshots are byte-identical to before.
3. `grep -rn "xLarge" overrides/app --include="*.tsx"` returns only `index.tsx`'s type union and `index.stories.tsx` — **confirmed zero production consumers today**, so blast radius is nil. Re-run this before committing; if a consumer has appeared, stop.
4. `npm run audit:tokens` does not flag the new rem constant (it carries a `// audit-allow:` or `provisional` comment naming the Figma frame, matching `PANEL_MIN_NARROW`'s existing treatment in the same file).

schema.description:
Executes a given bash command and returns its output.

The working directory persists between commands, but shell state does not. The shell environment is initialized from the user's profile (bash or zsh).

IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user:

 - Read files: Use Read (NOT cat/head/tail)
 - Edit files: Use Edit (NOT sed/awk)
 - Write files: Use Write (NOT echo >/cat <<EOF)
 - Communication: Output text directly (NOT echo/printf)
While the Bash tool can do similar things, it’s better to use the built-in tools as they provide a better user experience and make it easier to review tool calls and give permission.

# Instructions
 - If your command will create new directories or files, first use this tool to run `ls` to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location.
 - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes in your command (e.g., cd "path with spaces/file.txt")

In particular, never prepend `cd <current-directory>` to a `git` command — `git` already operates on the current working tree, and the compound triggers a permission prompt.
 - You may specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes). By default, your command will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
 - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes. You do not need to use '&' at the end of the command when using this parameter.
 - For git commands:
  - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
  - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
  - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.
 - Avoid unnecessary `sleep` commands:
  - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
  - Use the Monitor tool to stream events from a background process (each stdout line is a notification). For one-shot "wait until done," use Bash with run_in_background instead.
  - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — use `run_in_background`. No sleep needed.
  - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause.

 - When running `find`, search from `.` (or a specific path), not `/` — scanning the full filesystem can exhaust system resources on large trees.
 - When using `find -regex` with alternation, put the longest alternative first. Example: use `'.*\.\(tsx\|ts\)'` not `'.*\.\(ts\|tsx\)'` — the second form silently skips `.tsx` files.


# Committing changes with git

Only create commits when requested by the user. If unclear, ask first. When the user asks you to create a new git commit, follow these steps carefully:

You can call multiple tools in a single response. When multiple independent pieces of information are requested and all commands are likely to succeed, run multiple tool calls in parallel for optimal performance. The numbered steps below indicate which commands should be batched in parallel.

Git Safety Protocol:
- NEVER update the git config
- NEVER run destructive git commands (push --force, reset --hard, checkout ., restore ., clean -f, branch -D) unless the user explicitly requests these actions. Taking unauthorized destructive actions is unhelpful and can result in lost work, so it's best to ONLY run these commands when given direct instructions 
- NEVER skip hooks (--no-verify, --no-gpg-sign, etc) unless the user explicitly requests it
- NEVER run force push to main/master, warn the user if they request it
- CRITICAL: Always create NEW commits rather than amending, unless the user explicitly requests a git amend. When a pre-commit hook fails, the commit did NOT happen — so --amend would modify the PREVIOUS commit, which may result in destroying work or losing previous changes. Instead, after hook failure, fix the issue, re-stage, and create a NEW commit
- When staging files, prefer adding specific files by name rather than using "git add -A" or "git add .", which can accidentally include sensitive files (.env, credentials) or large binaries
- NEVER commit changes unless the user explicitly asks you to. It is VERY IMPORTANT to only commit when explicitly asked, otherwise the user will feel that you are being too proactive

Copy (Figma leading, per the cards): single message uses the **product-named** variant, "Cloud 91 Small Clutch added to Wishlist"; already-in-wishlist is "An item in your bag already exists in Wishlist"; max-reached is "An item in your bag has reached maximum quantity". The generic stacked variant ("Item added to Wishlist") is only reachable once 404 lands with real stacking — a toast has no aggregation concept and is always on its own from the shopper's point of view, so the **interim toast uses the product-named copy**. Both divergences from SFCC-272's AC wording go on the deferred Jira comment; the cards are not edited.

**Pass criteria.**
1. `grep -rn "useToast\|toast(" overrides/app/pages/cart overrides/app/components/ui-kits/**/zimmCart*` shows exactly **one** emit site.

#### Step 4.4 — `ZimmCartItemActions` + pending-item-across-auth

Note the actions are **not** inside base `product-item` — it receives them as a `secondaryActions` prop from its caller. So this molecule is supplied by the container, and we do not fight the base structure to inject it.

Remove: item removed, drawer count decrements, totals update; quantity > 1 removes all units in one action.

Wishlist, guest: the existing `ZimmWishlistAuthDrawer` via `useWishlistAuthDrawer`, **one hook instance**, `intentId: 'cart-wishlist'`. The `.docs/prd/cart.md` §2 paraphrase is the weaker justification and should not be the one cited.

Pending item held in **React state** (covers email-code and create-account, where the page never unloads) **and** session storage (covers the Apple/Google redirect). Read state first, fall back to storage, clear **both** together. Same **5-minute** age bound as the hook's own intent (`PENDING_WISHLIST_INTENT_MAX_AGE_MS`), so a stale item cannot be resumed.

Rejected and not to be revisited: one hook instance per line item (mounts a `useForm`, three `useAuthHelper`s, a `useAuthModal` and a drawer **per row** — a ten-item bag mounts ten of each, against a stated mobile-page-speed priority); adding an optional `itemId` to the shared `PendingWishlistIntent` (better long-term, but changes a shared hook with three existing call sites — raise separately).

| 15 | `feat(cart): SFCC-272 ZimmCartItemActions and pending-item resume` | 4.4 |
| 16 | `feat(cart): SFCC-272 ZimmCartEmptyState` | 4.5 |
| 17 | `feat(cart): SFCC-275 ZimmCartButtonGroup and Pay marks` | 5.1 |
| 18 | `feat(cart): SFCC-315 wire the drawer trigger in _app and product-view` | §9 |

`commit-msg` enforces conventional format and `/generate-changelog` depends on it, so every message
is `type(scope): SFCC-NNN description`.

**Two things this ordering buys:**

- **Commit 18 puts the trigger last.** Under §2 it had to ship with B1. Here nothing is reachable
  until everything is built, and the review reads as "here is the thing, here is where we plug it
  in." A genuine gain from the single-PR shape.
- **Commit 4 preserves the copy-first pause intact.** Copy-first was never about branching — it is
  about not bundling the override copy with functional change. Commit 4 stops and waits for
  Marcel to observe all eight markers from the cart, the account wishlist page and a checkout
  summary. Nothing proceeds until that is recorded.

## Loop, restated per commit group

§5's per-step Tester/Scorer criteria stand verbatim. Only the per-branch scaling is replaced:

| Commits | Loop |
|---|---|
| 1 | None. Verified by reading `detect-changes`'s output on the next cart PR. |
| 2, 3 | Light — a path check and a width assertion. |
| 4 | **Mandatory human stop.** The one step a machine cannot score alone. |
| 5–11 | Full loop. Largest surface: ~25 ACs including 11 accessibility. |
| 12–16 | Full loop, and **commit 13 gets the only adversarial pass** — concurrency, double-write, server rejection, boundary at 2/3/4/5, and proving `useIsMutating()` by making it fail on purpose first. |
| 17, 18 | Light on 17. **18 carries a regression check**, not a light pass: `product-view` is consumed by the PDP, the quick-view modal and the bonus-product modal, and 18 changes their add-to-bag feedback. |

## Costs accepted by choosing one PR

1. **No PR-time E2E on this PR.** `detect-changes` computes `e2e_scope` from the diff. Ours includes
   `_app/`, `product-item/`, `item-variant/`, `icons/`, `assets/` and `qa.yml` — none in the `cart`
   allow-list — so it resolves to **`skip`**. Commit 1 helps the *next* cart PR, not this one.
   This build ships on unit tests and Storybook only. Under §2, B0 landing first would have given
   B3/B4/B5 coverage.
2. **Four reviewer groups on one PR** — `@tier-1-approvers` (`qa.yml`), `@tier-2-approvers`
   (`_app/`, `product-item/`, `theme/components/index.ts`), `@pwa-squad-a` and `@pwa-squad-b`;
   plus manually-requested reviewers for the three ungoverned files (`item-variant/`,
   `useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts`, `useCartDrawer.ts`).
3. **Hard Rule #10 squarely engaged** — one change spanning Tier 1 CI/CD, Tier 2 Global Shell,
   Tier 2 Shared Product, Tier 2 theme registration, Tier 3 recipes and untiered code. Authorised:
   `marcelannavarro` verified in `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers` and repo `admin`, scope confirmed
   by him as the developer.
4. **Revert granularity is the whole cart.** If SIT surfaces a problem, the revert is all seven
   stories. Mitigated by the eighteen scoped commits, which allow a targeted revert instead.
5. **Zephyr build naming will be meaningless.** `computeBuildName.mjs` derives the name from a PR's
   *primary* Jira key; seven keys have no primary. Cosmetic, but it will read wrong in the
   dashboard. `e2e-browserstack-preview`'s `--grep` OR-joins all seven keys correctly, so scoping
   still works.

## PR body requirement

A ~60-file, seven-story PR is unverifiable without a body that maps **story → commits → files →
ACs**. That is `zimmerMANNPostBuild`'s deliverable and it is real work — budget it rather than
discover it at the end. Note the recorded PR-body standard says *no SFCC key in the title* while
every recent PR carries one; settle which before opening.

392	enabled; at max → `+` disabled/greyed; fully OOS or unavailable → **both** disabled/greyed); error
393	state (red inline message beneath the stepper — OOS, Partially OOS, Unavailable, copy supplied);
394	promotional price ("Was $X" / "Now $Y" replacing standard price, plus a discount label beneath the

400	  explicit reason for bundling. Consequence to accept: the ACs can't be signed off independently and
401	  Zephyr will count the same coverage from three keys.

403	  SFCC-282, Unavailable to SFCC-796 — both Sprint 6, Tech design, Hazel's. Build the states
404	  prop-driven with stories; not provable end to end this sprint.

406	  with `listPrice`/`currentPrice`/`isOnSale`, renders `ListPrice` for the struck value, and already
407	  multiplies by quantity (`price={listPrice * quantity}`) so it is line-item aware. `cart.md` CAI-013
408	  confirms sale was/now is in scope and price-book sourced. **Only the discount label is new, and it
409	  is purely presentational** — prop-driven, storied, wired when the promotions engine lands.

411	  use the bridge pattern (faithful default export, styling in a recipe).

414	  — 44×44 is 2.1 **AAA**, and `AGENTS.md`'s standard is 2.2 AA. **Decision: inherit the existing 24px**,
415	  add an inline comment naming 795's AC and the mislabelling per the house pattern in §2.15, and add
416	  it to the UI designer's open list alongside the hover contrast (2.96:1) and inverse focus ring
417	  already there. Growing the atom would hit every icon button in the app.

420	
421	ACs — Remove (3): item removed with drawer count decrementing and totals updating; removing the last
422	item shows the empty state "as per SFCC-277"; quantity > 1 removes all units in one action.
423	Wishlist (5): authenticated qty 1 → moved, removed from cart, count decrements, totals update,
424	**page-level success banner** "[Product Name] has been moved to your wishlist"; authenticated qty > 1
425	→ all units removed, a single SKU saved, count decrements by the full quantity, same banner;

462	  file.
463	- **Jira: no AC edits.** PO-approved cards are not edited — document via a comment instead.
464	- **Disclosure of a silent change: explicitly out of scope** (Marcel, this session). Not to be
465	  re-raised.

9	 * Copy-first port of node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/product-item/index.jsx
10	 * (retail-react-app 10.0.0), converted to TypeScript per AGENTS.md's copy-first rule (SFCC-270,
11	 * plan step 2.1). Zero functional diff at that step — TypeScript annotations, the import path
12	 * rewrites documented below, and a temporary `[overrides]` console.log marker (verified live
13	 * against three real surfaces per the plan's copy-first stop, then removed) were the only
14	 * changes; styling/behaviour changes are this commit (plan step 2.2, see below), not that one.
15	 *
16	 * Import path rewrites, per .claude/rules/overrideStyling.md's "Importing an already-overridden
17	 * component from a new component":
18	 * - `item-variant` / `item-variant/item-image` / `item-variant/item-name` /
19	 *   `item-variant/item-attributes` / `item-variant/item-price`: this repo overrides all five
20	 *   (SFCC-270, this same commit), so these are relative imports rather than the base
21	 *   `@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` path — a base-path import here would silently exercise the
22	 *   unstyled base components in Storybook/Vitest instead of these overrides.
23	 * - `./bonus-product-quantity` / `./product-quantity-picker`: same reasoning, both overridden in
24	 *   this same commit, in this same folder.
25	 * - `responsive` (`HideOnDesktop`/`HideOnMobile`): also already overridden in this repo
26	 *   (overrides/app/components/responsive/index.tsx) — and not just a styling port, a genuine
27	 *   behavioural difference (it moves the mobile/desktop split to Chakra's `md` breakpoint instead
28	 *   of the base's `lg`) — so this is rewritten to a relative import too, for the same reason.
29	 * - `shared/ui`, `loading-spinner`, `utils/utils`, and the `app/hooks` barrel (`useCurrency`/
30	 *   `useDerivedProduct`) are NOT overridden anywhere in this repo (verified by directory listing
31	 *   at time of writing) — these stay on the base `@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` path, since
32	 *   there is no local override to redirect to.
33	 *
34	 * `SfccProduct` is kept as `any` with a named alias rather than a structural type invented from
35	 * usage — this package ships no TypeScript types for this shape, matching the same documented gap
36	 * at overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx:136-151.
37	 *
38	 * SFCC-270 (plan step 2.2): restyled to the Figma cart-item spec via product-item.css.ts's
39	 * `ZimmCartItem` recipe (`row`/`details`/`info` parts, applied through `sx` — see that recipe's
40	 * own docblock for why `sx`, not `__css`, is required on a plain Flex/Stack here). The image's
41	 * own default width moved out of this file entirely — item-image.tsx now supplies its own
42	 * responsive default via item-variant.css.ts's `image` part, so the `mr`-based gap this file
43	 * used to add is replaced by the `row` part's own Figma-specified `gap`.
44	 * `CartItemVariantAttributes` now also renders with `combineAttributeValues`, per the Figma
45	 * spec's single "colour, size" string (see that component's own file). The two `display={[...]}`
46	 * responsive-array primaryAction visibility toggles are replaced with this file's own already-
47	 * imported `HideOnMobile`/`HideOnDesktop` (both already used here for `deliveryActions`) — the
48	 * original arrays split at Chakra's default `sm` (480px), one breakpoint earlier than this
49	 * file's own `md` (768px) split everywhere else; no Figma value distinguishes this, so it is
50	 * unified to the same `md` split as the rest of this file rather than preserved as a second,
51	 * unexplained breakpoint — flagged in this build's report as a disclosed interpretation, not a
52	 * tested requirement.
53	 *
54	 * Gift-card *detection* is still NOT implemented — unchanged finding from the prior round: no
55	 * real signal for "this line item is a digital gift card" exists anywhere in this codebase or
56	 * the commerce SDK types at time of writing (`GiftCertificateItem` exists in the SDK but is a
57	 * structurally different, wholly separate basket line-item shape that this component's own
58	 * render tree — `useDerivedProduct`, `ItemVariantProvider`'s `SfccProduct` shape — is not built
59	 * to receive at all). That finding stands as-is; it was independently confirmed by two separate
60	 * reviewers in the prior round and is not re-litigated here.
61	 *
62	 * SFCC-270 round 2 rework: the *capability* half is now built. `hideStepperAndActions` (optional,
63	 * defaults falsy so every existing caller is unaffected) suppresses the quantity stepper
64	 * (BonusProductQuantity/ProductQuantityPicker) and every actions surface (primaryAction,
65	 * secondaryActions, deliveryActions) when true, per .claude/session-notes.md §11.2's gift-card
66	 * variant note ("no stepper, no actions ... build ZimmCartItem with the stepper and actions row
67	 * optional"). Nothing else in this component's render tree branches on it — the 5-field
68	 * label/value block that same note describes for a real gift-card line item is not built here,
69	 * and remains for whichever future commit ends up owning real gift-card detection.
70	 *
71	 * SFCC-795 (plan step 3.2): `message` (optional, prop-driven) renders a ZimmInlineMessage between
72	 * the quantity stepper and the actions row, per .claude/session-notes.md §11.2 ("inline message
73	 * (error/warning) sits between the stepper and the actions"). This component does not itself
74	 * determine OOS/partial-OOS/unavailable/max-quantity state — OOS/partial-OOS detection is
75	 * SFCC-282's, "Unavailable" detection is SFCC-796's, both later-sprint tickets. Undefined (every
76	 * existing caller today) renders nothing and leaves the Item Details gap at its existing 12px
77	 * desktop value (`ZimmCartItem`'s `hasError` resolution prop, product-item.css.ts, derived below
78	 * from `message?.variant === 'error'`).
79	 */
80	import React from 'react';
81	
82	// Chakra Components
83	import {
84	  Box,
85	  Fade,
86	  Flex,
87	  Stack,
88	  Text,
89	  useMultiStyleConfig,
90	} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/shared/ui';
91	
92	// Project Components
93	import { HideOnDesktop, HideOnMobile } from '../responsive';
94	import ItemVariantProvider from '../item-variant';
95	import CartItemVariantImage from '../item-variant/item-image';
96	import CartItemVariantName from '../item-variant/item-name';
97	import CartItemVariantAttributes from '../item-variant/item-attributes';
98	import CartItemVariantPrice from '../item-variant/item-price';
99	import LoadingSpinner from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/loading-spinner';
100	import BonusProductQuantity from './bonus-product-quantity';
101	import ProductQuantityPicker from './product-quantity-picker';
102	import { ZimmInlineMessage } from 'app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmInlineMessage';
103	
104	// Hooks
105	import { useCurrency, useDerivedProduct } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks';
106	
107	const ZIMM_CART_ITEM_RECIPE = 'ZimmCartItem';
108	
109	type SfccProduct = any;
110	
111	type ProductItemProps = {
112	  product: SfccProduct;
113	  primaryAction?: React.ReactNode;
114	  secondaryActions?: React.ReactNode;
115	  deliveryActions?: React.ReactNode;
116	  onItemQuantityChange?: (quantity: number) => any;
117	  /**
118	   * Declared on the base file's propTypes but never read inside this component's own render
119	   * body — kept here only to mirror that declared surface one-for-one (zero functional diff,
120	   * SFCC-270). No return-type guarantee to derive from PropTypes.func, so typed loosely.
121	   */
122	  onAddItemToCart?: (...args: any[]) => any;
123	  showLoading?: boolean;
124	  /** Declared on the base file's propTypes but never read inside this component's own render body — see onAddItemToCart above. */
125	  isWishlistItem?: boolean;
126	  containerStyles?: Record<string, any>;
127	  isRemoving?: boolean;
128	  pickupInStore?: boolean;
129	  /**
130	   * Gift-card capability slot (SFCC-270 round 2 rework, session-notes.md §11.2): when true,
131	   * suppresses the quantity stepper and every actions surface (primaryAction, secondaryActions,
132	   * deliveryActions). Defaults falsy so every existing caller's rendering is unchanged. This
133	   * component does not itself detect a gift-card line item — see this file's own docblock — a
134	   * caller sets this explicitly once real detection exists.
135	   */
136	  hideStepperAndActions?: boolean;
137	  /**
138	   * Cart-line inline status message (SFCC-795 §11.2, plan step 3.2), rendered via
139	   * ZimmInlineMessage between the quantity stepper and the actions row. Presentation only — see
140	   * ZimmInlineMessage's own docblock: this component does not itself determine OOS/partial-OOS/
141	   * unavailable/max-quantity state, a caller passes the already-resolved variant + copy.
142	   * Undefined (the default for every existing caller) renders nothing and leaves the Item
143	   * Details gap at its existing 12px desktop value.
144	   */
145	  message?: {
146	    variant: 'error' | 'warning';
147	    text: string;
148	  };
149	};
150	
151	/**
152	 * Component representing a product item usually in a list with details about the product - name, variant, pricing, etc.
153	 * @param {Object} product Product to be represented in the list item.
154	 * @param {node} primaryAction Child component representing the most prominent action to be performed by the user.
155	 * @param {node} secondaryActions Child component representing the other actions relevant to the product to be performed by the user.
156	 * @param {node} deliveryActions Child component representing the delivery actions relevant to the product to be performed by the user.
157	 * @param {func} onItemQuantityChange callback function to be invoked whenever item quantity changes.
158	 * @param {boolean} showLoading Renders a loading spinner with overlay if set to true.
159	 * @returns A JSX element representing product item in a list (eg: wishlist, cart, etc).
160	 */
161	const ProductItem = ({
162	  product,
163	  primaryAction,
164	  secondaryActions,
165	  deliveryActions,
166	  // CodeRabbit (SFCC-11 cumulative review): default was `noop`, a synchronous no-op returning
167	  // `undefined` - but product-quantity-picker.tsx's handleQuantityChange unconditionally calls
168	  // `.then(...)` on this callback's return value. A caller that omits this optional prop and
169	  // then changes quantity would throw. This default resolves to `true` (a valid change) so the
170	  // `.then` chain completes normally instead.
171	  onItemQuantityChange = async () => true,
172	  showLoading = false,
173	  containerStyles = {},
174	  isRemoving = false,
175	  pickupInStore = false,
176	  hideStepperAndActions = false,
177	  message,
178	}: ProductItemProps) => {
179	  const { stepQuantity, showInventoryMessage, inventoryMessage, quantity, setQuantity } = useDerivedProduct(
180	    product,
181	    false,
182	    false,
183	    pickupInStore,
184	  );
185	  const { currency: activeCurrency } = useCurrency();
186	  // hasError drives ZimmCartItem's own Item Details gap widening (12px -> 16px desktop) — see
187	  // product-item.css.ts's docblock — derived from `message`, not a separate prop, so the two can
188	  // never disagree about whether an error-variant message is currently showing.
189	  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_CART_ITEM_RECIPE, { hasError: message?.variant === 'error' });
190	  return (
191	    <Box position="relative" data-testid={`sf-cart-item-${product.productId ? product.productId : product.id}`}>
192	      <ItemVariantProvider variant={product}>
193	        {showLoading && <LoadingSpinner />}
194	        <Stack layerStyle="cardBordered" align="flex-start" {...containerStyles}>
195	          <Flex sx={styles.row} width="full" backgroundColor="white">
196	            <CartItemVariantImage />
197	            <Stack sx={styles.details} flex={1}>
198	              <Flex sx={styles.info}>
199	                <Stack spacing={1}>
200	                  <CartItemVariantName />
201	                  <CartItemVariantAttributes excludeBonusLabel combineAttributeValues />
202	                  <HideOnDesktop>
203	                    <Box marginTop={2}>
204	                      <CartItemVariantPrice align="left" currency={activeCurrency} />
205	                    </Box>
206	                  </HideOnDesktop>
207	                </Stack>
208	                {!hideStepperAndActions && deliveryActions && !product.bonusProductLineItem && (
209	                  <HideOnMobile>{deliveryActions}</HideOnMobile>
210	                )}
211	              </Flex>
212	
213	              {!hideStepperAndActions && deliveryActions && !product.bonusProductLineItem && (
214	                <HideOnDesktop>{deliveryActions}</HideOnDesktop>
215	              )}
216	
217	              <Flex align="flex-end" justify="space-between">
218	                <Stack spacing={1}>
219	                  {!hideStepperAndActions &&
220	                    !(isRemoving && product.bonusProductLineItem) &&
221	                    (product.bonusProductLineItem ? (
222	                      <BonusProductQuantity product={product} />
223	                    ) : (
224	                      <ProductQuantityPicker
225	                        product={product}
226	                        onItemQuantityChange={onItemQuantityChange}
227	                        stepQuantity={stepQuantity}
228	                        quantity={quantity}
229	                        setQuantity={setQuantity}
230	                      />
231	                    ))}
232	                </Stack>
233	                <Stack>
234	                  <HideOnMobile>
235	                    <CartItemVariantPrice currency={activeCurrency} />
236	                  </HideOnMobile>
237	                  {!hideStepperAndActions && <HideOnMobile>{primaryAction}</HideOnMobile>}
238	                </Stack>
239	              </Flex>
240	
241	              {/* SFCC-795 §11.2: sits between the stepper (above) and the actions row (the
242	                  existing inventory Box below, secondaryActions, and the mobile primaryAction
243	                  block further down) — prop-driven only, see this file's own docblock. */}
244	              {message && <ZimmInlineMessage variant={message.variant} text={message.text} />}
245	
246	              <Box>
247	                {product && showInventoryMessage && (
248	                  <Fade in={true}>
249	                    <Text color="orange.600" fontWeight={600}>
250	                      {inventoryMessage}
251	                    </Text>
252	                  </Fade>
253	                )}
254	              </Box>
255	
256	              {!hideStepperAndActions && secondaryActions}
257	            </Stack>
258	          </Flex>
259	
260	          {!hideStepperAndActions && (
261	            <HideOnDesktop>
262	              <Box w={'full'}>{primaryAction}</Box>
263	            </HideOnDesktop>
264	          )}
265	        </Stack>
266	      </ItemVariantProvider>
267	    </Box>
268	  );
269	};
270	
271	export default ProductItem;
272

8	/*

10	 * (retail-react-app 10.0.0), converted to TypeScript per AGENTS.md's copy-first rule (SFCC-270,

14	 * omitted argument is implicitly `undefined` at runtime too — same value, just spelled out so it

21	 */
22	import React, { createContext, useContext } from 'react';
23	
24	/**
25	 * This component and associated context/hook provide a convenient wrapper
26	 * around a group of components used for rendering product variant details.
27	 */
28	
29	type SfccVariant = any;
30	
31	const ItemVariantContext = createContext<SfccVariant>(undefined);
32	
33	export const useItemVariant = (): SfccVariant => {
34	  return useContext(ItemVariantContext);
35	};
36	
37	type ItemVariantProviderProps = {
38	  // CodeRabbit (SFCC-11 cumulative review): was `variant?:` - an omitted variant flows straight
39	  // into context as `undefined`, and consumers (ItemPrice/ItemName, via useItemVariant) destructure
40	  // properties off it unguarded, which would throw on render. Required instead: the only real
41	  // caller (product-item/index.tsx) always passes `product`, itself a required prop - a pure
42	  // type-level tightening, no runtime behaviour change for any existing caller.
43	  variant: SfccVariant;
44	  children?: React.ReactNode;
45	};
46	
47	/**
48	 * The Provider component for rendering product item and variant detail.
49	 */
50	const ItemVariantProvider = ({ variant, children }: ItemVariantProviderProps) => {
51	  return <ItemVariantContext.Provider value={variant}>{children}</ItemVariantContext.Provider>;
52	};
53	
54	export default ItemVariantProvider;

8	import React from 'react'
9	import PropTypes from 'prop-types'
10	import {Box} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/shared/ui'
11	import CurrentPrice from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/display-price/current-price'
12	import ListPrice from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/display-price/list-price'
13	
14	/**
15	 * @param priceData - price info extracted from a product
16	 * // If a product is a set,
17	 *      on PLP, Show From X where X is the lowest of its children
18	 *      on PDP, Show From X where X is the lowest of its children and
19	 *          the set children will have it own price as From X (cross) Y
20	 * // if a product is a master
21	 *      on PLP and PDP, show From X (cross) Y , the X and Y are
22	 *          current and list price of variant that has the lowest price (including promotionalPrice)
23	 * // if a standard/bundle
24	 *      show exact price on PLP and PDP as X (cross) Y
25	 * @param currency - currency
26	 * @param quantity - quantity to take into the account for price display
27	 * @param currentPriceProps - extra props to be passing to CurrentPrice component
28	 * @param listPriceProps - extra props to be passing to ListPrice component
29	 * @param labelForA11y - label to be used for a11y
30	 */
31	const DisplayPrice = ({
32	    labelForA11y,
33	    priceData,
34	    currency,
35	    quantity = 1,
36	    currentPriceProps = {},
37	    listPriceProps = {}
38	}) => {
39	    const {listPrice, currentPrice, isASet, isMaster, isOnSale, isRange} = priceData
40	    const renderCurrentPrice = (isRange) => (
41	        <CurrentPrice
42	            labelForA11y={labelForA11y}
43	            price={currentPrice * quantity}
44	            as="b"
45	            currency={currency}
46	            isRange={isRange}
47	            {...currentPriceProps}
48	        />
49	    )
50	
51	    const renderListPrice = (isRange) =>
52	        listPrice && (
53	            <ListPrice
54	                labelForA11y={labelForA11y}
55	                currency={currency}
56	                price={listPrice * quantity}
57	                isRange={isRange}
58	                {...listPriceProps}
59	            />
60	        )
61	
62	    const renderPriceSet = (isRange) => (
63	        <>
64	            {renderCurrentPrice(isRange)} {isOnSale && renderListPrice(isRange)}
65	        </>
66	    )
67	
68	    if (isASet) {
69	        return renderCurrentPrice(true)
70	    }
71	
72	    if (isMaster) {
73	        return renderPriceSet(isRange)
74	    }
75	
76	    return <Box>{renderPriceSet(false)}</Box>
77	}
78	
79	DisplayPrice.propTypes = {
80	    priceData: PropTypes.shape({
81	        currentPrice: PropTypes.number.isRequired,
82	        isOnSale: PropTypes.bool.isRequired,
83	        listPrice: PropTypes.number,
84	        pricePerUnit: PropTypes.number,
85	        isASet: PropTypes.bool,
86	        isMaster: PropTypes.bool,
87	        isRange: PropTypes.bool,
88	        maxPrice: PropTypes.number,
89	        tieredPrice: PropTypes.number
90	    }),
91	    currency: PropTypes.string.isRequired,
92	    labelForA11y: PropTypes.string,
93	    currentPriceProps: PropTypes.object,
94	    listPriceProps: PropTypes.object,
95	    quantity: PropTypes.number
96	}
97	
98	export default DisplayPrice

1	/**
2	 * Commerce/ProductItem — Storybook stories for the cart line-item shell (SFCC-270, plan
3	 * step 2.2), restyled to the Figma cart-item spec.
4	 *
5	 * Providers supplied by .storybook/preview.tsx: IntlProvider, ChakraProvider.
6	 * This file adds its own inert provider stack, matching product-view/index.stories.tsx's own
7	 * documented pattern (see that file for the full rationale):
8	 *   MemoryRouter — item-name.tsx's <Link> (react-router-dom) and useMultiSite (via
9	 *     MultiSiteProvider below) both need Router/site context.
10	 *   MultiSiteProvider — useMultiSite (item-name.tsx's <Link>'s buildUrl, and
11	 *     StoreLocatorProvider below, which reads the current site to namespace its localStorage key).
12	 *   StoreLocatorProvider — `useDerivedProduct` (via item-price.tsx/item-attributes.tsx's own
13	 *     transitive dependency chain) unconditionally calls `useSelectedStore()`
14	 *     (`use-selected-store.js`), which throws `'useSelectedStore must be used within a
15	 *     StoreLocatorProvider'` with no Provider present — round 2 rework fix, confirmed by reading
16	 *     that hook's source, not assumed. Nested inside MultiSiteProvider (its own body calls
17	 *     useMultiSite()), outside CommerceProviders (its one consumer, `useSelectedStore`'s internal
18	 *     `useStores` call, resolves with `enabled: false` here since no story sets a selected store
19	 *     in localStorage, so it never actually needs Commerce context — but this file nests it
20	 *     inside CommerceProviders anyway for a single consistent provider order). `config={{}}` is a
21	 *     deliberately empty stand-in — no story here drives real store-locator state, so there is no
22	 *     real config value to supply; PropTypes will warn on the missing required fields, which is
23	 *     inert noise, not a render failure.
24	 *   CommerceApiProvider + QueryClientProvider — item-attributes.tsx's usePromotions/
25	 *     useProducts/useProduct/useCurrentBasket (via
26	 *     `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-current-basket`). `disableAuthInit` +
27	 *     an `.invalid` proxy URL prevent any real network calls; none of this story's mock line
28	 *     items carry priceAdjustments/bundledProductItems/type.bundle, so every one of those
29	 *     hooks resolves with `enabled: false` and never actually fetches.
30	 *   CurrencyProvider — useCurrency (item-price.tsx, product-item/index.tsx itself).
31	 *   ServerContext.Provider (from `@salesforce/pwa-kit-react-sdk`, not commerce-sdk-react) —
32	 *     found live in Storybook, not anticipated: item-attributes.tsx's useCurrentBasket() call
33	 *     above has its own separate transitive chain (useSFPayments -> useAppOrigin -> useOrigin)
34	 *     that calls the SDK's useServerContext() and destructures `res` from it unconditionally.
35	 *     With no Provider, useContext returns undefined and the destructure throws before useOrigin's
36	 *     own `typeof window !== 'undefined'` branch (which never touches `res` at all) is reached.
37	 *     `value={{}}` matches exactly what the real app's own browser bootstrap supplies
38	 *     client-side (`ssr/browser/main.js`'s `OuterApp`) — confirmed by reading that file.
39	 *
40	 * `GiftCard` story (round 2 rework): renders `ProductItem` with the new `hideStepperAndActions`
41	 * prop (SFCC-270 round 2, session-notes.md §11.2) set to true, on a plausible mock line item —
42	 * NOT a real gift-card detection, which this build still cannot do (see index.tsx's own docblock;
43	 * unchanged finding from the prior round). This story demonstrates the capability half only:
44	 * that when a caller explicitly asks to hide the stepper/actions, neither renders.
45	 */
46	import type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/react-webpack5';
47	import { fn } from 'storybook/test';
48	import React from 'react';
49	import { MemoryRouter } from 'react-router-dom';
50	import { QueryClient, QueryClientProvider } from '@tanstack/react-query';
51	import { CommerceApiProvider } from '@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react';
52	import { CurrencyProvider, MultiSiteProvider, StoreLocatorProvider } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/contexts';
53	import { ServerContext } from '@salesforce/pwa-kit-react-sdk/ssr/universal/contexts';
54	import ProductItem from '.';
55	
56	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
57	// Commerce provider stack (inert — no real API calls). See product-view/index.stories.tsx.
58	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
59	const storybookQueryClient = new QueryClient({
60	  defaultOptions: { queries: { retry: false, refetchOnWindowFocus: false } },
61	});
62	
63	const CommerceProviders = ({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) => (
64	  <QueryClientProvider client={storybookQueryClient}>
65	    <CommerceApiProvider
66	      clientId="00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"
67	      organizationId="f_ecom_storybook_001"
68	      shortCode="storybook"
69	      siteId="ZimmermannAU"
70	      locale="en-AU"
71	      currency="AUD"
72	      proxy="https://storybook.invalid/mobify/proxy/api"
73	      redirectURI="https://storybook.invalid/callback"
74	      disableAuthInit
75	      silenceWarnings
76	    >
77	      <CurrencyProvider currency="AUD">{children}</CurrencyProvider>
78	    </CommerceApiProvider>
79	  </QueryClientProvider>
80	);
81	
82	const WithProviders = (Story: React.ComponentType) => (
83	  <ServerContext.Provider value={{}}>
84	    <MemoryRouter>
85	      <MultiSiteProvider site={{ id: 'ZimmermannAU' }} buildUrl={(path: string) => path}>
86	        <StoreLocatorProvider config={{}}>
87	          <CommerceProviders>
88	            <Story />
89	          </CommerceProviders>
90	        </StoreLocatorProvider>
91	      </MultiSiteProvider>
92	    </MemoryRouter>
93	  </ServerContext.Provider>
94	);

96	// Data-URI SVG at the item-image `image` part's own ~2:3 ratio — no network needed, keeps

98	const lineItemImage = (fill: string) => ({

106	// CartItemVariantAttributes' own `combineAttributeValues` into "Lilac Sand, One Size".
107	const MOCK_LINE_ITEM = {

109	  productId: '25595021M',
110	  id: '25595021M',
111	  productName: 'Lilac Sand Silk Midi Dress',

113	  price: 495,

115	  pricePerUnit: 495,
116	  quantity: 1,
117	  stepQuantity: 1,
118	  minOrderQuantity: 1,
119	  imageGroups: [{ viewType: 'small', images: [lineItemImage('f6f4f1')] }],
120	  variationAttributes: [

122	    { id: 'size', name: 'Size', values: [{ value: 'ONESIZE', name: 'One Size', orderable: true }] },
123	  ],
124	  variationValues: { color: 'JJ5FUXX', size: 'ONESIZE' },
125	  // Round 2 rework fix: useVariationAttributes' isVariantValueOrderable (base SFCC hook, called
126	  // unconditionally via useDerivedProduct) does `product.variants.filter(...)` with no guard —
127	  // an undefined `variants` throws. Empty array is enough: nothing in this story asserts
128	  // orderability, it only needs to not crash (confirmed by reading that hook's source).
129	  variants: [],
130	};
131	
132	const MOCK_LINE_ITEM_TWO = {
133	  ...MOCK_LINE_ITEM,
134	  itemId: 'b2c3d4e5f6a1b2c3d4e5f6a1',
135	  productId: '25601452M',
136	  id: '25601452M',
137	  productName: 'Ivory Linen Wide-Leg Trouser',
138	  name: 'Ivory Linen Wide-Leg Trouser',
139	  price: 395,
140	  priceAfterItemDiscount: 395,
141	  pricePerUnit: 395,
142	  quantity: 2,
143	  imageGroups: [{ viewType: 'small', images: [lineItemImage('f9f8f6')] }],
144	  variationAttributes: [
145	    { id: 'color', name: 'Colour', values: [{ value: 'IVR', name: 'Ivory', orderable: true }] },
146	    { id: 'size', name: 'Size', values: [{ value: '2', name: '2', orderable: true }] },
147	  ],
148	  variationValues: { color: 'IVR', size: '2' },
149	  variants: [],
150	};
151	
152	const meta: Meta<typeof ProductItem> = {
153	  title: 'Commerce/ProductItem',
154	  component: ProductItem,
155	  parameters: { layout: 'padded' },
156	  decorators: [WithProviders],
157	  args: {
158	    onItemQuantityChange: fn(async () => true),
159	  },
160	};
161	
162	export default meta;
163	type Story = StoryObj<typeof ProductItem>;
164	
165	export const Default: Story = {
166	  args: {
167	    product: MOCK_LINE_ITEM,
168	    primaryAction: <button type="button">Remove</button>,
169	  },
170	};
171	
172	export const MultipleItems: Story = {
173	  render: (args) => (
174	    <>
175	      <ProductItem {...args} product={MOCK_LINE_ITEM} primaryAction={<button type="button">Remove</button>} />
176	      <ProductItem {...args} product={MOCK_LINE_ITEM_TWO} primaryAction={<button type="button">Remove</button>} />
177	    </>
178	  ),
179	};
180	
181	// See this file's own docblock: demonstrates the `hideStepperAndActions` capability only, not
182	// real gift-card detection. `primaryAction`/`secondaryActions`/`deliveryActions` are still passed
183	// here deliberately, to prove they are suppressed by the prop rather than merely absent.
184	export const GiftCard: Story = {
185	  args: {
186	    product: MOCK_LINE_ITEM,
187	    primaryAction: <button type="button">Remove</button>,
188	    secondaryActions: <button type="button">Edit</button>,

8	import React from 'react'
9	import PropTypes from 'prop-types'
10	import {Text, VisuallyHidden} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/shared/ui'
11	import {useIntl} from 'react-intl'
12	import msg from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/display-price/messages'
13	/**
14	 * Component that displays list price of a product with a11y
15	 * @param currency - currency
16	 * @param price - price of the product
17	 * @param as - an HTML tag or component to be rendered as
18	 * @param isRange - show price as range or not
19	 * @param labelForA11y - label to be used for a11y
20	 * @param extraProps - extra props to be passed into Text Component
21	 * @returns {JSX.Element}
22	 */
23	const ListPrice = ({labelForA11y, price, isRange = false, as = 's', currency, ...extraProps}) => {
24	    const intl = useIntl()
25	    const listPriceText = intl.formatNumber(price, {
26	        style: 'currency',
27	        currency
28	    })
29	
30	    return (
31	        <>
32	            {isRange ? (
33	                <Text
34	                    as={as}
35	                    {...extraProps}
36	                    aria-label={intl.formatMessage(msg.ariaLabelListPriceWithRange, {
37	                        listPrice: listPriceText || ''
38	                    })}
39	                    color="gray.700"
40	                >
41	                    {listPriceText}
42	                </Text>
43	            ) : (
44	                <Text
45	                    as={as}
46	                    {...extraProps}
47	                    aria-label={intl.formatMessage(msg.ariaLabelListPrice, {
48	                        listPrice: listPriceText || ''
49	                    })}
50	                    color="gray.700"
51	                >
52	                    {listPriceText}
53	                </Text>
54	            )}
55	            {/*For screen reader, we want to make sure the product name is announced before the price to avoid confusion*/}

import type { SystemStyleObject } from '@chakra-ui/react';

/**
 * State the component feeds in so this recipe can resolve the Item Details gap widening for an
 * active error-variant ZimmInlineMessage (SFCC-795 §11.2, plan step 3.2). Named `hasError` (not
 * e.g. `isError`/`errorActive`) to match the resolution-prop convention already used by every
 * other function-form baseStyle in this codebase — zimmQuantityStepper.css.ts's own `disabled`
 * key, and that file's own comment on why: theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts's
 * PROP_COMBINATIONS harness only exercises the fixed key set `{inverse, disabled, hasError,
 * focused, filled}`, so a differently-named boolean here would never have its `true` branch
 * walked by that guard.
 */
export type ZimmCartItemStyleProps = {
  hasError?: boolean;
};

/**
 * Co-located recipe for the cart line-item shell (overrides/app/components/product-item).
 * SFCC-270 (plan step 2.2) — restyles the copy-first port to the Figma-sourced cart-item spec.
 *
 * Parts:
 *   - `row` — the image + item-details row. Figma: gap 28px desktop / 24px mobile, align
 *     centre desktop / start mobile.
 *   - `details` — the column beside the image (name/attrs/price/stepper/actions). Figma:
 *     gap 12px desktop / 24px mobile.
 *   - `info` — the name + colour/size (+ mobile price) block, paired with the desktop-only
 *     delivery-actions slot. Figma: column layout desktop / row + justify-space-between
 *     mobile. The mobile values match this block's pre-existing unconditional layout exactly
 *     (row, space-between, align flex-end) so nothing changes below `md` — only the desktop
 *     column switch is new.
 *
 * Applied via `sx`, not `__css`, though the two parts of this file's `Flex`/`Stack` pair get
 * there for different reasons — corrected here (round 2 rework) after reading both chunks
 * directly rather than assuming they behave alike:
 *   - `Stack` (`chunk-WKZT7ZXJ.mjs`) passes its own computed `alignItems`/`justifyContent`/
 *     `flexDirection`/`gap` as SEPARATE literal props ahead of `{...rest}` in its own render
 *     (`jsx(chakra.div, {..., alignItems: align, ..., gap: spacing, ...rest})`). Those land in
 *     `@chakra-ui/system`'s `toCSSObject` (`chunk-E32MZNBA.mjs`) `styleProps` tier —
 *     `assignAfter({}, __css, baseStyle, styleProps, sx)` — which sits ABOVE `__css`, so a
 *     `__css`-applied value from this recipe would be silently outranked by Stack's own `gap`
 *     whenever this component also sets one. `sx` (last, unconditionally winning) avoids that.
 *   - `Flex` (`chunk-MPFPK3CX.mjs`) does NOT do the same thing — it does not pass `align`/
 *     `justify`/`direction` as separate literal props at all. It bundles all of them into ONE
 *     `__css` object, placed BEFORE `{...rest}` (`jsx(chakra.div, {ref, __css: styles, ...rest})`).
 *     That is the same silent-full-object-discard mechanism `item-variant.css.ts`'s own docblock
 *     documents for `Text` — a later same-named key in one object literal replaces the earlier
 *     one, it does not merge — just with the winner reversed: a caller-supplied `__css` prop
 *     arriving via `rest` would silently discard Flex's OWN align/justify/direction/etc
 *     translation entirely, not the other way around. `sx` is a different prop name, so it never
 *     collides with either `__css` at this level — it flows through `rest` untouched and is
 *     merged in later, last, by the same `toCSSObject` call. Net effect for this file is
 *     unchanged either way: `sx` is safe and correct on both `Flex` and `Stack` here, regardless
 *     of which mechanism is in play.

 * (`var(--zimm-scale-s)`) by default, widening to 16px (`var(--zimm-scale-m)`) when an
 * error-variant ZimmInlineMessage is present, per `.claude/session-notes.md` §11.2 ("In error
 * states the Item Details gap widens 12 -> 16px"). Only the desktop step changes — the mobile
 * gap (24px, `var(--zimm-scale-xl)`) is untouched: the design record only calls out the desktop
 * value, and 24px already exceeds 16px, so there is nothing to "widen" on mobile. `baseStyle` is
 * therefore now a function of `hasError` (see `ZimmCartItemStyleProps` above) rather than the
 * plain object it was through SFCC-270 — `row`/`info` are unchanged and simply ignore the new
 * prop.
 */
export const ZimmCartItem = {
  parts: ['row', 'details', 'info'],
  baseStyle: ({ hasError = false }: ZimmCartItemStyleProps): Record<string, SystemStyleObject> => ({
    row: {
      flexDirection: 'row',
      alignItems: 'flex-start',
      gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)', // 24px mobile

        alignItems: 'center',
        gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-700)', // 28px desktop
      },
    },
    details: {
      gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)', // 24px mobile
      [`@media (min-width: ${breakpoints.md})`]: {
        // 16px (var(--zimm-scale-m) = foundation/spacing.ts's `m` = 1rem) when an error-variant

      justifyContent: 'space-between',
      alignItems: 'flex-end',
      [`@media (min-width: ${breakpoints.md})`]: {
        flexDirection: 'column',
        alignItems: 'flex-start',
        justifyContent: 'flex-start',
      },
    },
  }),
};

41	 * own default width moved out of this file entirely — item-image.tsx now supplies its own
42	 * responsive default via item-variant.css.ts's `image` part, so the `mr`-based gap this file

100	// Chakra Components
101	import {
102	  Box,
103	  Fade,
104	  Flex,
105	  Stack,
106	  Text,
107	  useMultiStyleConfig,
108	} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/shared/ui';
109	
110	// Project Components
111	import { HideOnDesktop, HideOnMobile } from '../responsive';
112	import ItemVariantProvider from '../item-variant';
113	import CartItemVariantImage from '../item-variant/item-image';
114	import CartItemVariantName from '../item-variant/item-name';
115	import CartItemVariantAttributes from '../item-variant/item-attributes';
116	import CartItemVariantPrice from '../item-variant/item-price';
117	import LoadingSpinner from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/loading-spinner';
118	import BonusProductQuantity from './bonus-product-quantity';
119	import ProductQuantityPicker from './product-quantity-picker';
120	import { ZimmInlineMessage } from 'app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmInlineMessage';
121	
122	// Hooks
123	import { useCurrency, useDerivedProduct } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks';
124	
125	const ZIMM_CART_ITEM_RECIPE = 'ZimmCartItem';
126	
127	type SfccProduct = any;
128	
129	type ProductItemProps = {
130	  product: SfccProduct;
131	  primaryAction?: React.ReactNode;
132	  secondaryActions?: React.ReactNode;
133	  deliveryActions?: React.ReactNode;
134	  onItemQuantityChange?: (quantity: number) => any;
135	  /**
136	   * Declared on the base file's propTypes but never read inside this component's own render
137	   * body — kept here only to mirror that declared surface one-for-one (zero functional diff,
138	   * SFCC-270). No return-type guarantee to derive from PropTypes.func, so typed loosely.
139	   */
140	  onAddItemToCart?: (...args: any[]) => any;
141	  showLoading?: boolean;
142	  /** Declared on the base file's propTypes but never read inside this component's own render body — see onAddItemToCart above. */
143	  isWishlistItem?: boolean;
144	  containerStyles?: Record<string, any>;
145	  isRemoving?: boolean;
146	  pickupInStore?: boolean;
147	  /**
148	   * Gift-card capability slot (SFCC-270 round 2 rework, session-notes.md §11.2): when true,
149	   * suppresses the quantity stepper and every actions surface (primaryAction, secondaryActions,
150	   * deliveryActions). Defaults falsy so every existing caller's rendering is unchanged. This
151	   * component does not itself detect a gift-card line item — see this file's own docblock — a
152	   * caller sets this explicitly once real detection exists.
153	   */
154	  hideStepperAndActions?: boolean;
155	  /**
156	   * Cart-line inline status message (SFCC-795 §11.2, plan step 3.2), rendered via
157	   * ZimmInlineMessage between the quantity stepper and the actions row. Presentation only — see
158	   * ZimmInlineMessage's own docblock: this component does not itself determine OOS/partial-OOS/
159	   * unavailable/max-quantity state, a caller passes the already-resolved variant + copy.
160	   * Undefined (the default for every existing caller) renders nothing and leaves the Item
161	   * Details gap at its existing 12px desktop value.
162	   */
163	  message?: {
164	    variant: 'error' | 'warning';
165	    text: string;
166	  };
167	  /**
168	   * Discount label rendered beneath the quantity stepper (SFCC-795 §4/§11.2, plan step 3.3),
169	   * e.g. "20% off applied". Purely presentational — this component does not compute or derive a
170	   * discount percentage/label itself; a caller passes the already-resolved string once the
171	   * promotions engine is wired (not yet, this sprint — see this file's own docblock). Undefined
172	   * (every existing caller today) renders nothing — no empty node is emitted.
173	   *
174	   * Styling: `textStyle="caption"` + `color="var(--zimm-color-text-secondary)"`, matching
175	   * item-variant.css.ts's `colourSize` part (the "Lilac Sand, One size" caption in this same
176	   * card) — the nearest existing sibling treatment. No Figma node or type style is cited
177	   * anywhere in .claude/session-notes.md for this specific element (searched directly for
178	   * "discount", not assumed) — PROVISIONAL pending UI-designer confirmation, same disclosure
179	   * pattern as zimmQuantityStepper.css.ts:35-38's `value` part and zimmButton.css.ts:244's
180	   * `BTN_MIN_WIDTH_LG`.
181	   */
182	  discountLabel?: string;
183	};
184	
185	/**
186	 * Component representing a product item usually in a list with details about the product - name, variant, pricing, etc.
187	 * @param {Object} product Product to be represented in the list item.
188	 * @param {node} primaryAction Child component representing the most prominent action to be performed by the user.
189	 * @param {node} secondaryActions Child component representing the other actions relevant to the product to be performed by the user.
190	 * @param {node} deliveryActions Child component representing the delivery actions relevant to the product to be performed by the user.
191	 * @param {func} onItemQuantityChange callback function to be invoked whenever item quantity changes.
192	 * @param {boolean} showLoading Renders a loading spinner with overlay if set to true.
193	 * @returns A JSX element representing product item in a list (eg: wishlist, cart, etc).
194	 */
195	const ProductItem = ({
196	  product,
197	  primaryAction,
198	  secondaryActions,
199	  deliveryActions,
200	  // CodeRabbit (SFCC-11 cumulative review): default was `noop`, a synchronous no-op returning
201	  // `undefined` - but product-quantity-picker.tsx's handleQuantityChange unconditionally calls
202	  // `.then(...)` on this callback's return value. A caller that omits this optional prop and
203	  // then changes quantity would throw. This default resolves to `true` (a valid change) so the
204	  // `.then` chain completes normally instead.
205	  onItemQuantityChange = async () => true,
206	  showLoading = false,
207	  containerStyles = {},
208	  isRemoving = false,
209	  pickupInStore = false,
210	  hideStepperAndActions = false,
211	  message,
212	  discountLabel,
213	}: ProductItemProps) => {
214	  const { stepQuantity, showInventoryMessage, inventoryMessage, quantity, setQuantity } = useDerivedProduct(
215	    product,
216	    false,
217	    false,
218	    pickupInStore,
219	  );
220	  const { currency: activeCurrency } = useCurrency();
221	  // hasError drives ZimmCartItem's own Item Details gap widening (12px -> 16px desktop) — see
222	  // product-item.css.ts's docblock — derived from `message`, not a separate prop, so the two can
223	  // never disagree about whether an error-variant message is currently showing.
224	  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_CART_ITEM_RECIPE, { hasError: message?.variant === 'error' });
225	  return (
226	    <Box position="relative" data-testid={`sf-cart-item-${product.productId ? product.productId : product.id}`}>
227	      <ItemVariantProvider variant={product}>
228	        {showLoading && <LoadingSpinner />}
229	        <Stack layerStyle="cardBordered" align="flex-start" {...containerStyles}>
230	          <Flex sx={styles.row} width="full" backgroundColor="white">
231	            <CartItemVariantImage />
232	            <Stack sx={styles.details} flex={1}>
233	              <Flex sx={styles.info}>
234	                <Stack spacing={1}>
235	                  <CartItemVariantName />
236	                  <CartItemVariantAttributes excludeBonusLabel combineAttributeValues />
237	                  <HideOnDesktop>
238	                    <Box marginTop={2}>
239	                      <CartItemVariantPrice align="left" currency={activeCurrency} />
240	                    </Box>
241	                  </HideOnDesktop>
242	                </Stack>
243	                {!hideStepperAndActions && deliveryActions && !product.bonusProductLineItem && (
244	                  <HideOnMobile>{deliveryActions}</HideOnMobile>
245	                )}
246	              </Flex>
247	
248	              {!hideStepperAndActions && deliveryActions && !product.bonusProductLineItem && (
249	                <HideOnDesktop>{deliveryActions}</HideOnDesktop>
250	              )}
251	
252	              <Flex align="flex-end" justify="space-between">
253	                <Stack spacing={1}>
254	                  {!hideStepperAndActions &&
255	                    !(isRemoving && product.bonusProductLineItem) &&
256	                    (product.bonusProductLineItem ? (
257	                      <BonusProductQuantity product={product} />
258	                    ) : (
259	                      <ProductQuantityPicker
260	                        product={product}
261	                        onItemQuantityChange={onItemQuantityChange}
262	                        stepQuantity={stepQuantity}
263	                        quantity={quantity}
264	                        setQuantity={setQuantity}
265	                      />
266	                    ))}
267	                </Stack>
268	                <Stack>
269	                  <HideOnMobile>
270	                    <CartItemVariantPrice currency={activeCurrency} />
271	                  </HideOnMobile>
272	                  {!hideStepperAndActions && <HideOnMobile>{primaryAction}</HideOnMobile>}
273	                </Stack>
274	              </Flex>
275	
276	              {/* SFCC-795 (plan step 3.3): discount label, directly beneath the stepper/price row
277	                  above, ahead of the inline message below — prop-driven only, no empty node when
278	                  omitted. See the `discountLabel` prop's own JSDoc for the styling citation. */}
279	              {discountLabel && (
280	                <Text
281	                  textStyle="caption"
282	                  color="var(--zimm-color-text-secondary)"
283	                  data-testid="zimm-discount-label"
284	                >
285	                  {discountLabel}
286	                </Text>
287	              )}
288	
289	              {/* SFCC-795 §11.2: sits between the stepper (above) and the actions row (the
290	                  existing inventory Box below, secondaryActions, and the mobile primaryAction
291	                  block further down) — prop-driven only, see this file's own docblock. */}
292	              {message && <ZimmInlineMessage variant={message.variant} text={message.text} />}
293	
294	              <Box>
295	                {product && showInventoryMessage && (
296	                  <Fade in={true}>
297	                    <Text color="orange.600" fontWeight={600}>
298	                      {inventoryMessage}
299	                    </Text>
300	                  </Fade>
301	                )}
302	              </Box>
303	
304	              {!hideStepperAndActions && secondaryActions}
305	            </Stack>
306	          </Flex>
307	
308	          {!hideStepperAndActions && (
309	            <HideOnDesktop>
310	              <Box w={'full'}>{primaryAction}</Box>
311	            </HideOnDesktop>
312	          )}
313	        </Stack>
314	      </ItemVariantProvider>
315	    </Box>
316	  );
317	};
318	
319	export default ProductItem;

1	/**
2	 * SFCC-270 round 2 rework, extended post-rework (found live in Storybook by Marcel, not by this
3	 * suite). Proves three stacked bugs are actually fixed TOGETHER, not just that the symbols were
4	 * added:
5	 *   1. `useVariationAttributes` -> `isVariantValueOrderable` (base SFCC hook, unconditional
6	 *      `product.variants.filter(...)`) needs `variants` to be an array on the mock product.
7	 *   2. `useDerivedProduct` unconditionally calls `useSelectedStore()`, which throws without a
8	 *      real `StoreLocatorProvider` ancestor.
9	 *   3. `item-attributes.tsx`'s `useCurrentBasket()` call has its own separate transitive chain
10	 *      (`useSFPayments` -> `useAppOrigin` -> `useOrigin`) that calls the SDK's
11	 *      `useServerContext()` and destructures `res` from it unconditionally, before `useOrigin`'s
12	 *      own `typeof window !== 'undefined'` branch (which never touches `res`) is reached. This
13	 *      file previously mocked `useCurrentBasket` away entirely, which hid this bug completely —
14	 *      unmocked now so this suite actually exercises the real chain. `ServerContext.Provider`
15	 *      with `value={{}}` matches exactly what the real app's own browser bootstrap supplies
16	 *      client-side (`ssr/browser/main.js`'s `OuterApp`) — confirmed by reading that file.
17	 *
18	 * Deliberately does NOT use index.test.tsx's harness — that file mocks the whole
19	 * `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks` barrel's `useDerivedProduct`, which would hide both
20	 * bugs this file exists to catch. This renders through the real, unmocked `useDerivedProduct` ->
21	 * `useVariationAttributes` -> `isVariantValueOrderable` / `useSelectedStore` chain, with a real
22	 * `StoreLocatorProvider` ancestor.
23	 *
24	 * `useMultiSite` and `useCurrency` are still mocked, for a reason that has nothing to do with
25	 * this build's own logic: `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/contexts` (the barrel both
26	 * `MultiSiteProvider`/`CurrencyProvider` and `use-multi-site.js`/`use-currency.js` resolve
27	 * through) is a `.js` file containing inline JSX, which Vite's transform cannot parse as a
28	 * plain `.js` file — confirmed empirically (this file's first draft imported `MultiSiteProvider`
29	 * from that barrel directly and vitest failed at import-analysis on
30	 * `app/contexts/index.js:49`, not at any assertion). This is the same parse failure
31	 * item-variant/index.test.tsx's own docblock already documents and works around by mocking
32	 * `use-multi-site` instead of using a real `MultiSiteProvider`; extended here to `useCurrency`
33	 * for the same reason. `StoreLocatorProvider` itself is real: `use-selected-store.js` and
34	 * `store-locator-provider.jsx` both import `StoreLocatorContext` via that file's own direct path
35	 * (`.../app/contexts/store-locator-provider`), never through the barrel, so it never hits this
36	 * parse wall — confirmed by reading both files' imports, not assumed.
37	 *
38	 * Two more pragmatic mocks, both explained inline at their own `vi.mock`/`beforeEach`: `useStores`
39	 * (an unrelated dual-module-instance QueryClient issue, not this build's own code) and a
40	 * `window.matchMedia` polyfill (jsdom has none; item-price.tsx's `useBreakpointValue` needs it —
41	 * the same pre-existing gap and fix product-item/index.test.tsx's own `beforeEach` already uses).
42	 * Neither affects what this file actually proves: that a real `StoreLocatorProvider` ancestor and
43	 * an array-valued `variants` together stop the render from throwing.
44	 */
